top.title: Inter handed injury scare as Manuel Akanji leaves Switzerland squad early due to muscular fatigue ahead of Atalanta clash
top.description: FBL-EUR-NATIONS-SLO-SUI - AFP Inter defender Manuel Akanji has withdrawn from the Switzerland squad following an injury scare during the international break. The experienced centre-back is set to return to Italy immediately to undergo an assessment by the Nerazzurri medical staff. International break cut short Akanji has officially departed the Switzerland national team camp ahead of their upcoming Nations League fixture against Scotland on Monday night. The defender has been granted permission to return to Inter several days earlier than originally anticipated following concerns regarding his physical condition. The 31-year-old was a key figure for his country on Friday evening, completing the full 90 minutes during a hard-fought 0-0 draw away to Slovenia. According to reports from Sky Sport Italia , the decision to release Akanji from international duty was made purely on precautionary grounds. While he will miss the match against the Scots, his early return to Milan is designed to ensure he receives the necessary recovery time at his club's training base. Crucial cog in Inter's machine The news will come as a slight worry for Cristian Chivu, who has relied heavily on the former Manchester City man throughout the opening months of the 2026-27 campaign . Akanji has established himself as an almost permanent fixture in the Nerazzurri backline, starting 12 of the club's 15 competitive fixtures across all competitions. His importance to the Italian champions is underlined by his playing time, with only goalkeeper Josep Martinez and midfield engine Nicolo Barella having clocked more minutes for the side so far this season. He has started nine of Inter's 11 Serie A matches and appeared in the starting XI for three of their four Champions League ties. Focus turns to Atalanta Despite the current alarm, there is optimism within the Inter camp that Akanji - who initially joined the club on loan in September 2025 before making the move permanent in July 2026 - will be available for selection when the Nerazzurri travel to Bergamo to face Atalanta on November 22. The Nerazzurri will be eager to have the experienced defender fully fit as they continue to push hard in the title race. Inter currently sit second in the Serie A standings with 28 points, trailing league leaders Lazio by just a single point. Switzerland aim to finish dominant campaign in style Switzerland currently sit comfortably at the summit of League B, Group 1, with 13 points to their name, holding a commanding five-point advantage over second-placed Slovenia. Having already secured promotion to League A regardless of the outcome against Scotland, the Swiss will look to round off their campaign in style, having comfortably beaten the Scots 3-0 in the reverse fixture in Glasgow.

top.title: Hope cross country teams sweep regional titles for first time; women hold off Calvin by 1 point
top.description: The Hope College cross country teams made history, racing to both the men's and women's NCAA regional championships. It was the first time in program history that both teams won regionals in the same year. The Hope women won the Great Lakes Regional title with 84 points, holing off Calvin by a single point on Saturday, Nov. 14, in East Lansing, and beating the entire 35-team field. The women's regional title also was Hope's eighth, joining teams from 2021, 2017, 2015, 2012, 1987, 1986, and 1985. More: Hope men's cross country reaches national for first time in 45 years after regional title "All you have to do is look at the score and you can see it was an exciting race," Hope coach Mark Northuis said. "Our women came through. They battled, and it just shows again that it's definitely a team race and our top five really came through only 15 seconds separating our top five. That's an amazing feat and made the difference for us today." Sophomore Anna Sybenga set the pace for the Flying Dutch, breaking into the top 10 in 10th place at 22:20.0. Senior Mary England was right on her heels in 13th at 22:24.4, while freshman Ruth Miller kept the momentum rolling with a 16th-place finish in 22:29.4. Senior Olivia Ippel and sophomore Miranda Sawvel closed out Hope's scoring pack by crossing the finish line just two-tenths of a second apart. Ippel secured 22nd place in 22:34.6, immediately followed by Sawvel in 23rd at 22:34.8. "They ran great as a group," Northuis said. "We put three freshmen out there, and they performed phenomenally. Ruthie Miller just came through running third for us on this team and that's just amazing for someone who wasn't even in our Top 12 a couple weeks ago. It's been fun to watch her develop and the other ladies who are right with them." Meanwhile, the men made it back-to-back regional titles, besting the 38-team field. Hope finished with 82 points, 29 points ahead of runner-up Calvin University. Case Western Reserve University placed third with 123 points. "That was our goal all year, along with winning the conference. The guys just came through," head coach Mark Northuis said after the Flying Dutch also earned the third men's regional title in program history, joining the 2025 and 1980 teams. top.title: Russia excluded from men's under-20 ice hockey worlds in Canada
top.description: FILE PHOTO - Russia's goalkeeper Andrei Vasilevskiy fails to save during the 2019 IIHF Ice Hockey World Championship Bronze medal match between Russia and Czech Republic at the Ondrej Nepela Arena. (is associated with: «Russia excluded from men's under-20 ice hockey worlds in Canada») Vít Šimánek/CTK/dpa The men's junior ice hockey world championship in Canada will take place without Russia, the sport's governing body said on Sunday. Canada, the host of the under-20 tournament, had announced that it did not plan to grant visas to Russia's team despite a recent Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruling saying Russia could return to international ice hockey. The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) had tried to exclude Russia on security grounds after a blanket sport ban due to the Ukraine war was phased out. "The IIHF confirms that due to the position and restrictions formally communicated by the Canadian Government, the Russian U20 national team is unable to participate in the World Junior Championship," a statement said. "After carefully assessing the feasibility of alternative arrangements, the IIHF Council has determined that Canada will remain as host and the tournament will proceed from 26 December 2026 to 5 January 2027 in Edmonton and Red Deer." It is still unclear what consequences the CAS ruling will have for the men's ice hockey world championship in May in Germany. The German government may follow Canada's lead after teams and sponsors threatened a boycott. The German Ice Hockey Federation welcomed the decision on the junior worlds. "For our U20 team, the situation is now clear. That gives players and the coaching team the necessary peace for preparation, which begins in a few weeks," chairman Frank Lutz said in a statement. "The Canadian government has clearly taken a position, and many nations have shown their stance in recent weeks. We now also need to plan securely for our home world championship in May - for the teams, the fans and all partners. We therefore demand a timely clarification from the IIHF."

top.title: Customs to review Police Unit’s container escort mandate — Adeniyi
top.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) is considering a review of the mandate of its Customs Police Unit (CPU), particularly its responsibility for escorting containers in transit, following the adoption of advanced technology for cargo monitoring. The Comptroller-General of Customs, Mr. Adewale Adeniyi, disclosed this at the Customs Police Unit Summit, which concluded in Abuja at the weekend. Adeniyi said the Service had acquired technology capable of monitoring containers from seaports to their destinations, including dry ports in the hinterland, making it necessary to reassess some of the unit’s traditional responsibilities. He recalled that the inauguration of the unit in 2019 generated agitation and resentment among some personnel, partly because of concerns about its assigned responsibilities. With technology providing more effective ways of monitoring cargo in transit, he said, the time had come to review the unit’s mandate and identify duties that could be performed more efficiently through modern systems. The Customs boss also stressed the need for collaboration with other security agencies and anti-corruption bodies, noting that effective Customs policing required expertise in intelligence gathering, surveillance, risk analysis and modern investigative techniques. He urged officers to respect human rights, observe due process and ensure the proper treatment of suspects. CPU must uphold integrity Addressing personnel of the unit, Adeniyi charged them to uphold discipline, restraint and integrity, describing these values as essential to protecting the reputation of the Service. “The red that you wear carries the trust of Nigerians and the reputation of the Service. Wear it with discipline, wear it with restraint, wear it with pride,” he said. He urged Customs officers to stay ahead of smugglers through intelligence-led operations, technology deployment and professionalism, warning that criminal networks were becoming increasingly sophisticated. According to him, the growing sophistication of criminal networks requires smarter enforcement strategies rather than continued reliance on conventional methods. “Criminal networks have grown more sophisticated. They use the same routes as legitimate traders to move firearm components, narcotics, fake medicines, protected wildlife and illicit funds, often through digital channels. Our answers must be smarter; they must not be harder,” he said. Adeniyi called for a more professional, accountable and technology-driven Customs Police Unit capable of addressing emerging security threats, combating illicit trade, strengthening institutional integrity and protecting the nation’s borders. top.title: Everything Dan Campbell said about Aidan Hutchinson’s injury
top.description: MUNICH, GERMANY - NOVEMBER 15: Aidan Hutchinson of Detroit Lions receives medical attention after going down with an injury while celebrating getting a sack during the NFL match between the New England Patriots and the Detroit Lions at the Allianz Arena on November 15, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Adam Pretty/Getty Images) | Getty Images We still don’t have a firm update on Aidan Hutchinson after he suffered an injury celebrating a first-down sack in the Detroit Lions’ Week 10 win over the New England Patriots . However, Lions coach Dan Campbell was asked several questions about the situation, even though he didn’t provide an exactly diagnosis. What’s the latest update on Aidan Huthcinson? Hutchinson was initially listed as questionable with a knee injury, then downgraded to out in the second half. Campbell would not offer up any additional information. “Nothing new. We’ll know more when we get back in the States,” Campbell said. “But anytime you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate that he is, he’s a captain of ours, that doesn’t make things easy. But I thought guys stepped up in his wake and showed up for us today and helped us out.” Does Hutchinson’s injury put a damper on the win over the Patriots? Campbell: “Anytime you lose a player like that and you don’t know the entirety of it–but knowing Hutch for who he is. It’s like he doesn’t stay down long. It does, it hurts a little bit, but as far as this game was concerned our guys stepped up and finished. We stayed strong. This is the second time this has happened—our guys have responded in a tough situation and didn’t bat an eye. Just went back to work, and that’s not easy to do. But, no, certainly you don’t want to know that a player like that is down.” What kind of depth do the Lions have? Detroit managed to create four more sacks on the day after Hutchinson’s injury—two by rookie Derrick Moore, one from Alim McNeill, and one from DJ Wonnum. Campbell expressed confidence in the Lions’ group of pass rushers, regardless of what Hutchinson’s ultimate diagnosis is. “We like ‘em,” Campbell said. “That’s why we applied them where we did. And I know this, Derrick Moore gets better every game. The more reps he gets, he gets better. It was good to get Wonnum back today. We know what Mac [McNeill] is, Sky(ler Gill-Howard). So can Tyleik (Williams). And all those guys, even Levi (Onwuzurike), (Tyler) Lacy, they play a different flavor, but they push the pocket, they got movement. But I think the important thing is, man, we knew we had to do to get out of this game with a win. We had to play really good defense. “And I really thought the back end played outstanding. We played some stick coverage today […] We’re improving. We gotta go. We gotta go. We’ll see where Hutch is at, but we’ve gotta step up now. We need some guys to really step up—and if that is the case (with a serious Hutchinson injury), fill that role.”

top.title: USC’s Playoff Hopes Crash After Late Turnover By Jayden Maiava
top.description: Wisconsin Badgers outside linebacker Sebastian Cheeks (15) sacks USC Trojans quarterback Jayden Maiava (14) during their game Oct. 24, 2026, at Camp Randall Stadium in Madison, Wisconsin. The USC Trojans’ dream of making the College Football Playoff died on a muddy field in Bloomington, Indiana. A promising drive that looked like it would tie the game ended with quarterback Jayden Maiava throwing a fatal interception. With six minutes and 35 seconds remaining at the one-yard line, Indiana’s Isaiah Jones intercepted the pass meant for Kayden Dixon-Wyatt. That single play killed the momentum for the No. 18 ranked Trojans and handed the No. 9 Hoosiers the win. USC lost 27-13 in a game filled with self-inflicted wounds. The Trojans dropped multiple interception opportunities, missed two field goals, and committed several penalties on special teams. The New York Post reported that these mistakes were especially perplexing since USC had just finished a second bye week during which coach Lincoln Riley vowed improved performance. Instead, the team converted only two of eleven third downs and faded badly in the fourth quarter. A Season of Missed Chances The loss to Indiana was a massive blow for a team that had just beaten then-No. 2 Ohio State two weeks earlier. The loss to Indiana likely ended any real shot at the playoff. Riley now sits at a record of 1-8 against ranked opponents on the road. Grant Wilson secured the victory for the Hoosiers by connecting with Charlie Becker on a 42-yard touchdown pass as three minutes and 30 seconds were left on the clock. USC simply could not answer the call when it mattered most. Questions for Lincoln Riley The pressure is now on USC athletics director Jen Cohen to decide if Riley is the right man to lead the program. The team had put itself on the clock with “The Time Is Now” billboards around Los Angeles, yet they failed to get it done. Following kicker Caden Chittenden’s missed 27-yard field goal to the right, Riley dropped his shoulders on the sideline. That miss ended a drive that had reached Indiana’s 8-yard line, leaving the Trojans stuck at a 20-13 deficit. The errors on special teams were just the latest in a long line of mistakes. The situation got even stranger when a fan ran onto the field during a timeout and made a field goal. This bizarre moment highlighted the chaos that consumed the Trojans’ night. Riley had vowed to fix the issues after a devastating road loss to Wisconsin earlier in the season, but the same problems returned with a vengeance. The Cost of Failure When a team has as much talent as USC, losing 27-13 to a top-10 opponent is hard to explain. The Trojans (7-3 overall, 4-3 Big Ten) simply could not make the big plays needed to win. Indiana (9-1, 6-1) controlled the game when it counted. The loss raises serious questions about the future of the program in Los Angeles. Riley fell to 1-8 against ranked teams on the road, a stat that does not look good for his job security.

top.title: YSU’s Regular Season Ends with Loss – What Awaits 8-3 Penguins on Selection Sunday?
top.description: Youngstown State’s regular season came to a somewhat unceremonious close on Saturday evening. Illinois State quarterback Beckham Pellant lowered his shoulder and dove over the goal line with just nine seconds left to lift the Redbirds to a gutsy 34-33 win over the Penguins. YSU has no game next weekend so that was it, at least for the regular season. With eight wins, Beau Brungard and company will still surely be in the playoffs when the bracket gets released next Sunday. But with no further chances to build their resume, the Penguins can only wait it out and see how the chips will fall. Where… and perhaps more importantly… when will they play next? That’s the question that looms over Doug Phillips’ team right now. There is an argument to be made that they’ve done enough to avoid playing Thanksgiving weekend but also plenty to suggest that the bye week may also no longer be a possibility either. Youngstown State is 8-3 with all of their victories coming over DI teams. They have ranked wins over South Dakota, Southern Illinois, Northern Iowa and North Dakota. Two of those were Top 10 victories at the time. With all that it’s probably safe to say that they haven’t played their last home game. Whether or not it’s in the first or second round, though, will largely depend on what some of their counterparts do this next Saturday. They will want the race for the top eight seeds to remain as open as possible and thus will need some squads who are in a similar spot to lose. YSU will be rooting for the following teams this weekend: Montana State (vs. Montana) South Dakota (@ Illinois State) Northern Colorado (@ Northern Arizona) ETSU (@ Mercer) Central Arkansas (vs. Austin Peay) McNeese (vs. Lamar) If those listed teams win that keeps the 5-8 seed range quite a bit clearer for the Penguins to grab one of those spots. If that comes to pass they’d be the only group to have two weeks off before their first playoff game. Whether or not that’s a good thing is a whole different conversation. In the scenario that they do end up playing in the opening round, one would imagine that they’d receiver a higher seed in the 9-12 range. That would guarantee a home game likely against a lower conference champion from somewhere like the Ohio Valley or Pioneer League. Last year Youngstown State drew Ivy League winner Yale in the first round and it’s a game their fans would probably rather just forget. A positioning like that would set up a potential matchup against a lower-seeded bye week team if they were to advance. A second-round road trip against the likes of a Lamar, Montana, Austin Peay or Mercer is entirely possible in that case. Closing it out against Illinois State would have gone a long way in avoiding all this speculation. As of now, though, Youngstown State has left much of its postseason fate into the hands of others and the committee. There will be more football to be played nonetheless, though, and they will not have to sweat it out as a bubble team next week.

top.title: Ronaldinho turns back the clock at 46 as the Brazil legend ends his 11-year exile with a stunning Ravenna comeback
top.description: Ravenna v Forli: Serie C - Getty Images Sport Ronaldinho turned back the clock on Sunday, ending 11 years away from professional football with a sensational comeback for Ravenna at the age of 46. The Brazil legend started the Serie C derby against Forli in front of a sold-out crowd, showed flashes of his old magic and played a key part in the opening goal before being substituted at half-time. Ronaldinho starts for Ravenna in Forli derby Ronaldinho made his long-awaited comeback on Sunday, starting for Ravenna in their Serie C derby against Forli at a sold-out Stadio Bruno Benelli. The Brazilian had not played since leaving Fluminense in 2015, and came out of retirement for the third-tier club he joined as an investor in August. According to BBC Sport, he trained with his new team-mates only once, on Saturday, before the game. A team graphic had placed him on the left, but he spent most of his 45 minutes in a central role. Ronaldinho plays key part in Donati opener There were plenty of bright touches from the former Barcelona star, and he was involved in the opening goal. Ronaldinho held off a defender before playing the pass that came before the assist for Giulio Donati, who drove in a shot from outside the box. He had already carved out an earlier chance for the defender, swinging in a corner that Donati met with a header, only to see it saved. Ronaldinho was then substituted at the break, ending an outing that was streamed in several countries around the world. Dida joins Ronaldinho amid half-time frenzy The interval brought a media circus, with journalists surrounding Ronaldinho, and Dida, his former team-mate with Brazil and AC Milan, joined him on the pitch. A temporary stand, named the R10 after his famous shirt number, had been built for the fixture. In his prime, Ronaldinho won the 2002 World Cup with Brazil, the 2006 Champions League with Barcelona, and league titles with Barca and Milan. He also claimed the Ballon d'Or and FIFA World Player of the Year award in 2005, and played for Paris Saint-Germain, Gremio, Flamengo, Atletico Mineiro, Fluminense and Queretaro. Will Ronaldinho play for Ravenna again? Ronaldinho scored 299 goals in his career and had hoped to reach 300 in Ravenna colours, with the plan being for him to take a penalty had the hosts been awarded one. Whether he gets another chance remains unclear, as it is not yet known if he will play again for Ravenna, who sit second in their Serie C group.

top.title: Ryan Preece Admits He Needs To Learn Heel-Toe From Shane Van Gisbergen
top.description: Greg Atkins-Imagn Images Ryan Preece knows he still has work to do on road courses. Preece told Yahoo Sports that he wants to learn how to heel-toe just like Shane Van Gisbergen. This admission shows a driver who is honest about his gaps and eager to improve his game. At Daytona International Speedway, 12 Ford Racing drivers gathered for the event on November 11. Preece partnered with Logan Sargeant for the Navy team. Robert Noaker and Austin Cindric stood out as the top contenders at the front. Ryan Blaney withdrew after a fall before the event, leading Noaker to step in. Repeated position swaps occurred between the leaders until Cindric executed a decisive pass with under five minutes left. Cindric secured victory by 0.136 seconds, while Preece claimed third and Sargeant finished fourth. Preece’s podium finish did not indicate he possessed the speed to challenge the leaders. He first had to work his way past Sargeant. By that stage, the top two had created sufficient separation to render a comeback improbable. Although the anti-lock braking system stopped the wheels from locking, Preece still needed to learn its response. Entering Daytona’s first turn, identifying the correct pressure and timing proved especially critical. His mention of heel-toe driving also warrants attention. During a downshift, this technique involves briefly blipping the throttle while braking. It aligns engine speed to maintain car balance. Mandatory Credit: Chuck Cook-USA TODAY Sports Josh Allen no longer has to share the top spot with Peyton Manning. The Buffalo Bills quarterback has officially moved ahead of the Pro Football Hall of Famer, becoming the NFL’s all-time leader in combined touchdowns by a quarterback through his first 10 seasons. And Allen has done it before completing his ninth year. And he did it in nine seasons. 😏 @JoshAllenQB | #BillsMafia pic.twitter.com/5PKNI0B5aX — Buffalo Bills (@BuffaloBills) November 15, 2026 Allen entered Sunday’s game against the New York Jets tied with Manning at 322 career touchdowns. One more touchdown was all he needed to claim the record for himself. On Buffalo’s second possession of the day, Allen methodically moved the Bills down the field. After a defensive holding call gave the Bills a first and goal at the one-foot line, Allen called his own number and used the opportunity to pass Manning. Josh Allen calls his own number. 😤 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/9Fj8amAJvc — Buffalo Bills (@BuffaloBills) November 15, 2026 With that touchdown, Allen’s career total climbed to 323, passing the mark Manning established during his first decade with the Indianapolis Colts. But the difference between the two quarterbacks isn’t just the number of touchdowns. It’s how quickly Allen got there. Manning needed 160 regular-season games to reach 322 touchdowns. Allen matched that total in just 136 games, throwing his record-tying touchdown against the Minnesota Vikings last Monday night. That’s 24 fewer games, the equivalent of nearly a season and a half of football. Allen has also taken a different route to the record. While Manning’s touchdowns came almost exclusively through the air, Allen has been just as dangerous with his legs. His career total entering Sunday included 232 passing touchdowns, 88 rushing touchdowns, and two receiving touchdowns. Patrick Mahomes is the only other active quarterback in the top 10 who can still add to his total. The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback entered Week 10 with 301 touchdowns and will spend the remainder of the season chasing Allen. But Mahomes is already in his 10th NFL season, meaning his final number will be set when the regular season ends in January. Allen, meanwhile, will have all of 2027 to keep adding to a record Mahomes will no longer be eligible to chase.

top.title: Mike Vrabel Delivers Blunt Message After Patriots' Blowout Loss to Lions: 'There's No Pep Talk'
top.description: Mike Vrabel Delivers Blunt Message After Patriots' Blowout Loss to Lions: 'There's No Pep Talk' originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . For the second week in a row, an NFC North team left the Patriots searching for answers. After falling to Green Bay in Week 9, New England continued its recent slide with a 35-10 loss to Detroit on Sunday. The Pats have now dropped three of their last four games and currently sit outside of the AFC playoff picture with a 5-5 overall record. To make matters worse, the Patriots added more players to their injury report, as quarterback Drake Maye (ankle) and wide receiver A.J. Brown (hamstring) left the game and didn't return. During his postgame press conference , New England coach Mike Vrabel told reporters that there is "no magic formula" to fix all of the team's issues. "There's no magic words. There's no pep talk," Vrabel said. "This is professional football. Do your job, line up, block them, tackle them, hit them, knock the ball loose, cover them, get open. "There's no magic formula. There's no pep talk I can go in there and give them right now that, in a week, we're gonna all of a sudden just be better. You gotta get back to work, and you gotta do it together." Vrabel made a comment about his players maintaining a "winner's mentality" because they will "figure out ways to help the team win" rather than "b— and complain." When asked if there are players who have complained, Vrabel clarified that he was speaking generally rather than pointing to a specific problem. "There's a lot of season left, and we know how these things go in the National Football League," Vrabel said. "But you're gonna have to start playing better, where we're at here in November." top.title: AJ Brown compared to one of New England Patriots’ worst ever NFL Draft picks after Lions loss
top.description: Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images The New England Patriots made a major move this offseason by trading a first-round pick for former Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver AJ Brown. The 29-year-old was expected to level up their offense and give Drake Maye an elite weapon in the passing game. However, Brown has had a quiet start in New England, recording just nine receptions for 101 yards and no touchdowns across three games. He struggled again in Sunday’s 35-10 defeat to the Detroit Lions in Munich, prompting Bill Simmons to make an unflattering comparison. Bill Simmons makes damning AJ Brown comparison after Patriots’ defeat to Lions AJ Brown’s difficult time in New England has been made worse by injuries, having already missed time this season due to knee and ankle problems. He returned for Sunday’s clash against Detroit in Germany but failed to make much of an impact before another setback ended his afternoon early. The former Eagles receiver has had fewer than 50 receiving yards in his first three Pats games and is yet to score a touchdown. His performances have already attracted criticism, and Bill Simmons was particularly unimpressed by what he saw against the Lions. The Patriots fan compared Brown to N’Keal Harry, who was selected with the 32nd overall pick in the first round of the 2019 NFL Draft. Simmons tweeted: “AJ Brown can’t even get open by one foot – it’s like having N’Keal Harry back.” Harry spent three seasons in New England before being released. He managed only four touchdowns for the Patriots and became one of the franchise’s biggest draft disappointments. Simmons also questioned why Mike Vrabel kept Brown on the field while trailing heavily against Detroit. He added: “Let’s keep a not-100% AJ Brown out there in a 28-3 game on a bad field; What could go wrong?” Brown eventually left the game in the fourth quarter after picking up a hamstring issue. The Patriots now have fresh injury concerns over two of their most important offensive players, as Drake Maye was also forced off early with an ankle problem .

nigeria.title: Customs to review Police Unit’s container escort mandate — Adeniyi
nigeria.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) is considering a review of the mandate of its Customs Police Unit (CPU), particularly its responsibility for escorting containers in transit, following the adoption of advanced technology for cargo monitoring. The Comptroller-General of Customs, Mr. Adewale Adeniyi, disclosed this at the Customs Police Unit Summit, which concluded in Abuja at the weekend. Adeniyi said the Service had acquired technology capable of monitoring containers from seaports to their destinations, including dry ports in the hinterland, making it necessary to reassess some of the unit’s traditional responsibilities. He recalled that the inauguration of the unit in 2019 generated agitation and resentment among some personnel, partly because of concerns about its assigned responsibilities. With technology providing more effective ways of monitoring cargo in transit, he said, the time had come to review the unit’s mandate and identify duties that could be performed more efficiently through modern systems. The Customs boss also stressed the need for collaboration with other security agencies and anti-corruption bodies, noting that effective Customs policing required expertise in intelligence gathering, surveillance, risk analysis and modern investigative techniques. He urged officers to respect human rights, observe due process and ensure the proper treatment of suspects. CPU must uphold integrity Addressing personnel of the unit, Adeniyi charged them to uphold discipline, restraint and integrity, describing these values as essential to protecting the reputation of the Service. “The red that you wear carries the trust of Nigerians and the reputation of the Service. Wear it with discipline, wear it with restraint, wear it with pride,” he said. He urged Customs officers to stay ahead of smugglers through intelligence-led operations, technology deployment and professionalism, warning that criminal networks were becoming increasingly sophisticated. According to him, the growing sophistication of criminal networks requires smarter enforcement strategies rather than continued reliance on conventional methods. “Criminal networks have grown more sophisticated. They use the same routes as legitimate traders to move firearm components, narcotics, fake medicines, protected wildlife and illicit funds, often through digital channels. Our answers must be smarter; they must not be harder,” he said. Adeniyi called for a more professional, accountable and technology-driven Customs Police Unit capable of addressing emerging security threats, combating illicit trade, strengthening institutional integrity and protecting the nation’s borders. nigeria.title: Gunmen kidnap three travellers, shoot driver on Benue highway
nigeria.description: By Peter Duru Armed men have reportedly kidnapped three travellers and shot a driver during an attack on a vehicle at Ijami village, Oglewu, Ohimini Local Government Area, LGA, of Benue State. The incident, which occurred at about 9:25pm on Saturday, involved seven persons travelling from Enugu to Abuja. The latest attack came barely days after a similar incident along the same axis, where a grieving man and his five friends were kidnapped while conveying the remains of his late wife from Kano for burial in neighbouring Okpokwu Local Government Area. In that incident, the kidnappers reportedly abandoned the corpse of the deceased on the highway before whisking her husband and his friends into the forest. They were subsequently released after a ransom was paid. Recounting the latest incident, an eyewitness, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the victims were attacked shortly after passing Otukpo on their way to Abuja. He said, “they were coming from Enugu and heading to Abuja on Saturday. At about 9:25pm, they got to a place called Ijami after Otukpo, under Oglewu. They were seven persons in the vehicle. The vehicle was attacked and the driver was shot. “He is in critical condition and currently receiving treatment in a hospital. Three of the passengers were taken into the forest by the armed men, while three of the passengers managed to escape. They have been seen and are in safe condition.” Expressing concern over the recurring attacks along the route, the eyewitness appealed to motorists to avoid travelling on the axis at night, blaming the deplorable condition of some roads for making it easier for criminals to operate. “We will continue to appeal to people to avoid these routes when night falls. Some of these roads are in deplorable condition, which makes it easy for the criminals to stop the vehicles and take away their victims. “We appeal that wherever you are coming from, pass the night in Otukpo and continue your trip the next day and be safe, rather than end up in the hands of armed men who will subject your family to unimaginable trauma to raise ransom money,” he said. Efforts to get the reaction of the Chairman of Ohimini Local Government Area, Gabriel Adole, were unsuccessful, as he did not respond to calls put across to his telephone. However, the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Peter Aondongu, confirmed the incident. He said, “The victims were seven in number, three were rescued while three others are with the kidnappers. The driver was shot and he is receiving treatment at Teaching Hospital, Otukpo. “While efforts are on to secure the release of the other three, we urge the commuters to avoid night travels. Whenever it is night, look for somewhere and pass the night. The Commissioner had issued that advice and we expect that people, for their own safety, desist from night travels.” Vanguard News The post Gunmen kidnap three travellers, shoot driver on Benue highway appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.description: The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council has disclosed that President Bola Tinubu’s proposed Five-Year Strategic Defence Operations Plan is ready, describing it as a major step towards tackling insecurity across the country. The council said the plan would strengthen Nigeria’s security architecture, improve military effectiveness and provide a coordinated response to terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and other criminal activities. In a statement issued on Sunday by its spokesperson, Dele Alake, the council said the initiative was designed to align defence priorities, operational requirements, capability development and expenditure with Nigeria’s current and anticipated security challenges. It described the plan as part of Tinubu’s determination to reposition the country’s security system towards a more coordinated, intelligence-led, technology-enabled and prevention-oriented framework. On military expansion, the statement disclosed that Tinubu had approved the creation of four new Army divisions and the restructuring of existing formations to expand operational coverage and improve responses to security threats. It added that the President had also approved the establishment of two additional Army depots in Osogbo, Osun State, and Amasiri-Edda, Ebonyi State, to increase military training capacity and accelerate the recruitment of soldiers. According to the council, the two facilities can accommodate 6,000 recruits each, giving them a combined capacity of 12,000 soldiers at a time. The Osogbo facility, it said, currently has 5,210 recruits undergoing training. The statement added that the expansion of the training facilities was expected to reduce recruitment turnaround time and increase the number of soldiers available for deployment. It further disclosed that Tinubu had approved the recruitment of an additional 28,000 soldiers to strengthen the military’s presence and improve operational effectiveness. The President was also said to have approved the recruitment of 50,000 additional police officers as part of efforts to reinforce internal security and improve the country’s policing capacity. The revered monarch warned that ethnicity, regional affiliations and differences in social backgrounds must never be allowed to undermine the unity of the Muslim Ummah or the collective responsibility of Nigerians to build a peaceful, stable and prosperous nation. He stressed that Muslims, irrespective of their ethnic origins or geographical locations, shared a common religious identity and must demonstrate, through their conduct and relationships, the unifying principles of Islam. The Sultan made the call on Sunday in Ibadan, Oyo State, while addressing participants at the 11th General Assembly of the Muslim Ummah of South-West Nigeria (MUSWEN), held at the M.O. Abdul Hall, University of Ibadan Central Mosque Auditorium. Ethnicity should never be a determining factor in identifying who is a Muslim and who is not. Almighty Allah created us as one human family and commanded us to worship Him alone and glorify His name,” the Sultan said. nigeria.title: 2027: Atiku storms Bauchi communities, questions Tinubu’s grassroots outreach
nigeria.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar weekend took his presidential campaign to communities across Bauchi State, drawing large crowds along his route from the airport to the Bauchi State Presidential Lodge and during a road trip to Azare. The tour, which featured a campaign rally, visits to four communities and courtesy calls on two traditional rulers, was part of his efforts to deepen grassroots engagement ahead of the 2027 general elections, while challenging President Bola Tinubu’s record of direct engagement with Nigerians. Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, said Atiku began the day’s engagements at 8am with consultations with stakeholders before proceeding to an 11am rally in Bauchi. Atiku thanked residents for the reception, saying it had strengthened his resolve to take his message of affordable living and responsible leadership to communities across the country. After the rally, his campaign train travelled by road to Azare, stopping in Soro, Kari, Darazo and Misau, where residents turned out to welcome him and his entourage. In Misau, Atiku paid a courtesy visit to the Emir, Alhaji Ahmed Suleiman, thanking him and his council for their hospitality and words of encouragement. He also acknowledged residents who waited to receive his entourage despite its arrival at nightfall. He arrived in Azare at 10.30pm, where he paid a courtesy visit to the Emir of Katagum, extending his engagements with traditional rulers and community leaders. The campaign team is expected to proceed to Potiskum on Sunday for another rally. However, the ADC campaign used the reported scale of the reception to question Tinubu’s grassroots engagement, challenging the President to demonstrate a similar willingness to meet Nigerians directly. “The scale of yesterday’s welcome raises a simple question: can the sitting President volunteer to meet the people and make even half the effort Atiku has made to reach them?” Shaibu said. nigeria.title: State Police: NASS to transmit bill to Tinubu this week -Senator Bamidele
nigeria.description: *Raises vital questions on the irresponsible use of social media *Receives ‘The Sun Senator of the Year’ Award *Dedicates award to God, President Tinubu, and 108 other senators By Henry Umoru ABUJA – LEADER of the Senate, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, APC, Ekiti Central has disclosed that the National Assembly will this week the State Police Bill to President Bola Tinubu for assent. He said the National Assembly is expecting four State Houses of Assembly to turn in their reports on or before the National Assembly reconvenes on November 17, 2026, saying with this development, next week is going to be decisive and defining in the National Assembly. Bamidele said whether the remaining states turn in their reports or not, the National must move forward and fulfil the aspiration of the people. According to Bamidele, the principle of proactive lawmaking guided the resolve of the National Assembly to pass the State Police (Constitution Alteration) Bill, which, according to him, proposed the creation of a Federal Police Service and State Police Services. The proposed constitutional amendment which is part of ongoing efforts to restructure Nigeria’s policing architecture by providing for the establishment of State Police Services, is intended to create the constitutional foundation for decentralised policing, amid continuing national discussions on how to strengthen security arrangements and improve responses to security challenges across the country. Bamidele spoke after he received “The Sun Senator of the Year” Award for efficiently managing the business of the parliament and for his proactive approach to lawmaking, which has guided all the undertakings of the Senate since its inauguration in June 2023. nigeria.description: The Trump administration said Sunday the air travel havoc triggered by a no-takeoff order could drag on for another day, pushing back its timetable for a return to normal. Hundreds more flights were cancelled and questions remained over how such chaos could unfold in the world’s largest economy, a country that prides itself on its technological prowess. Officials blame Friday’s huge snafu on faulty work to upgrade air traffic control communication cables. President Donald Trump on Sunday ended uncharacteristic days of silence on the ground stop, but only to blame his predecessor Joe Biden for the debacle. Trump insisted he inherited a mess from the Biden administration and said Congress, which his party has controlled for two years, must approve funds to upgrade America’s outdated air traffic control system. “The Biden Administration was an FAA disaster,” Trump said, referring to the Federal Aviation Administration. “Everything they touched turned bad. Big money spent unwisely, making an old and broken system worse than when they began,” Trump asserted. FAA chief Bryan Bedford had said Saturday that air travel for millions of Americans stranded at airports would return to normal by the close of business on Sunday. But Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Sunday morning it will actually take longer to get planes, crews and travelers to where they need to be. “So, in the airspace, we’re going to see things come back to normal today, but probably fully normal tomorrow,” Duffy said on ABC News. “We had airplanes and crews out of position because of Friday, so it takes a little bit of time to do that.” – ‘I’m the secretary’ – Duffy also flatly rejected calls for his resignation over the travel chaos, insisting he inherited woefully outdated air traffic control infrastructure, such as, he said, radar equipment that dates back to the 1960s. “So when we do work and things go wrong, of course I’m the secretary. But I also have to acknowledge what was delivered to me,” Duffy said in an interview on CNN. As of Sunday morning 1,460 flights within, into or out of the United States had been cancelled, according to the travel monitor site flightaware.com. The Trump administration has blamed Friday’s ground stop — meaning no planes can take off — on a botched replacement of old copper wire communication lines. Friday’s disruption was only the second time such a ground stop had been issued in US airspace, which is among the busiest in the world, since the 9/11 attacks. Duffy has appealed for $50 billion in funds to upgrade and modernize the air traffic control system, and called for Congress, which controls the purse strings of the US government, to “meet this moment.” But Democrats quickly pounced to say Congress under Trump’s Republicans could already have done this. nigeria.title: Guinea deports 1,557 West Africans in gold mining crackdown
nigeria.description: By Favour Ulebor & Agency Reports Guinea has expelled 1,557 West African nationals arrested and convicted for illegal gold mining as the government intensifies its crackdown on unauthorised mining activities across the country. Judicial and security sources told AFP on Sunday that the foreigners, mostly from Burkina Faso and Mali, were arrested at different mining sites during an operation against illegal mining. The deportees were transported in a convoy of 44 vehicles, which arrived in Kouremale, a border town between Guinea and Mali, on Saturday after leaving the capital, Conakry, on Friday. According to the sources, the foreigners were released and expelled after receiving prison sentences ranging from 18 months to two years. The Guinean government has increased operations against illegal gold mining since the beginning of November, particularly in Siguiri, a major gold-producing region in the northeastern part of the country. Authorities said the crackdown was aimed at stopping the illegal exploitation of mineral resources and reducing the environmental damage caused by unregulated mining. The operations have also affected thousands of West African migrants who travelled to Guinea in search of employment and better living conditions after fleeing poverty and insecurity in their home countries. Meanwhile, the crackdown has sparked tensions between miners and security forces. At least 10 people were killed on Wednesday following violent clashes between miners and security personnel in Siguiri, according to a government statement issued on Thursday. Reacting to the deaths, Guinea’s main opposition coalition on Saturday condemned what it described as an “authoritarian drift” and criticised the government’s use of force “as a method of government.” The latest expulsions come amid growing concerns over the treatment of migrant miners and the government’s efforts to control illegal mining activities. The move broke below Friday’s low of about $67,555 and marked the weakest level since mid-August, as weekend trading extended a selloff that has followed a stronger dollar and a fully priced December Federal Reserve rate hike. entertainment.title: Professor Patricia Mamko Lar Makes History as First Female Vice-Chancellor of UNIJOS
entertainment.description: Professor Patricia Mamko Lar, appointed as the 11th substantive Vice-Chancellor and first female Vice-Chancellor of the University of Jos. The University of Jos (UNIJOS) has officially appointed Professor Patricia Mamko Lar as its 11th substantive Vice-Chancellor, making her the first woman to occupy the position since the institution was established in 1971. Announced on Thursday, 12 November 2026 by the university’s Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of Council, Senator Grace Folashade Bent , during a special meeting of the 15th Governing Council, the historic appointment sees Professor Lar succeed Professor Tanko Ishaya as she takes the helm of the Plateau State institution. Born in Langtang, Plateau State, Professor Lar is a distinguished Professor of Medical Microbiology whose career has been deeply woven into the fabric of UNIJOS for nearly four decades. After earning her Bachelor of Science degree in Microbiology from Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria in 1986, she joined the University of Jos in 1987 as a Graduate Assistant in the Department of Medical Microbiology. She later went on to earn her Master’s degree in Medical Microbiology in 1989 and her PhD in Medical Parasitology in 1998 from the University of Lagos, followed by postdoctoral training at the Institute of Human Virology, University of Maryland in the United States under the NIH-Fogarty Fellowship Programme. Rising steadily through the academic ranks, she became an Associate Professor in 2012 before attaining full professorship in October 2015. Over the years, she has built an impressive body of work with more than 40 scholarly publications focusing on infectious diseases, including HIV/AIDS, malaria, antimicrobial resistance, and phytomedicine. Beyond the lecture hall and laboratory, Professor Lar has also served in key administrative roles at UNIJOS—including Head of the Department of Microbiology and Director of Linkages and Collaborations—and previously served a six-month tenure as Acting Vice-Chancellor of Yakubu Gowon University (formerly the University of Abuja) following her appointment by President Bola Tinubu in February 2025. Alongside her academic and leadership credentials, Professor Lar is a recognised advocate for women’s empowerment, having received the He4She Certificate of Award for Women Empowerment Activism in 2019. As she begins her five-year single term as UNIJOS’s first female substantive Vice-Chancellor after 55 years, she brings nearly four decades of institutional experience to the university’s top seat. entertainment.title: Ramla Ali Wins IBF and WBO Titles to Become Somalia’s First Boxing World Champion
entertainment.description: Unified world champion Ramla Ali poses in the ring with her WBO and IBF super-bantamweight belts and her coaching team in Arlington, Texas. Photo Credit: Yahya Ali/Instagram British-Somali boxer and fashion model Ramla Ali is officially a unified world champion! On 8 November 2026 at the College Park Center in Arlington, Texas, the 37-year-old athlete captured the vacant IBF and WBO super-bantamweight world titles after securing a split-decision victory over American contender Mikiah Kreps . During the ten-round bout, Ali dropped Kreps with a sharp right hand in the third round—the sole knockdown of the night—before two judges scored the contest 97–92 and 96–93 in her favour, against one scorecard of 98–91 for Kreps. With this triumph, Ali became Somalia’s first-ever professional boxing world champion and a unified titleholder in one unforgettable night. Born in Mogadishu, Somalia, she fled the civil war as a child with her family and grew up in East London, initially taking up boxing in secret as a teenager before turning it into a life-changing calling. Ramla Ali makes her ring walk behind the Somali and British flags ahead of her super-bantamweight world title fight in Arlington, Texas. Photo Credit: Yahya Ali/Instagram Her remarkable journey from refugee to Olympic athlete and champion is also the subject of the biographical feature film In the Shadows. Directed by Anthony Wonke , the film premiered at the 70th BFI London Film Festival on 9 October 2026 before opening in UK and Irish cinemas on 30 October—just over a week before she lifted her world title belts in Texas. BAFTA-winning Top Boy actress Jasmine Jobson stars as Ali alongside Peaky Blinders actor Finn Cole as her husband and former coach, Richard Moore , with both Ali and Moore serving as executive producers on the project. This championship milestone builds on a string of barrier-breaking firsts across sports, cinema, and fashion. Long before her title win in Arlington, Ali made history as the first Muslim woman to win an English amateur boxing title, the first boxer to win an international gold medal while representing Somalia, and the first boxer to represent Somalia on the Olympic stage when she competed in the women’s featherweight division at the Tokyo 2020 Summer Olympics. Ramla Ali celebrates in the ring as the referee raises her hand following her split-decision victory over Mikiah Kreps on 8 November 2026. Photo Credit: Yahya Ali/Instagram Away from the ring, she has carved out an equally notable space in global luxury fashion. Ali has graced the covers of British Vogue, Elle UK, Harper’s Bazaar Arabia, and Grazia UK, served as a brand ambassador for Cartier and Dior, and made history as the first boxer to wear custom ring attire created by major fashion houses—including bespoke fight kits designed by Dior, Off-White, Versace, Alexander McQueen, and Burberry featuring the panther emblem from Somalia’s coat of arms. Sworn in at the New Jersey Statehouse in Trenton on 9 November 2026, Emehelu has made double history in the process—becoming New Jersey’s first immigrant Lieutenant Governor and forming part of the state’s first all-women Governor–Lieutenant Governor team. Born in Nigeria before moving to the United States at the age of three, Emehelu brings an extraordinary record of public service and legal excellence to New Jersey’s second-highest executive office. Before this historic appointment, she served as Acting State Comptroller , leading key efforts to combat fraud, waste, and abuse while protecting taxpayer funds and strengthening government accountability, and also stepped in as Acting Secretary of State to oversee New Jersey’s elections. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. He has started nine of Inter's 11 Serie A matches and appeared in the starting XI for three of their four Champions League ties. The Nerazzurri will be eager to have the experienced defender fully fit as they continue to push hard in the title race. sports.title: Russia excluded from men's under-20 ice hockey worlds in Canada
sports.description: FILE PHOTO - Russia's goalkeeper Andrei Vasilevskiy fails to save during the 2019 IIHF Ice Hockey World Championship Bronze medal match between Russia and Czech Republic at the Ondrej Nepela Arena. (is associated with: «Russia excluded from men's under-20 ice hockey worlds in Canada») Vít Šimánek/CTK/dpa The men's junior ice hockey world championship in Canada will take place without Russia, the sport's governing body said on Sunday. Canada, the host of the under-20 tournament, had announced that it did not plan to grant visas to Russia's team despite a recent Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruling saying Russia could return to international ice hockey. The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) had tried to exclude Russia on security grounds after a blanket sport ban due to the Ukraine war was phased out. "The IIHF confirms that due to the position and restrictions formally communicated by the Canadian Government, the Russian U20 national team is unable to participate in the World Junior Championship," a statement said. "After carefully assessing the feasibility of alternative arrangements, the IIHF Council has determined that Canada will remain as host and the tournament will proceed from 26 December 2026 to 5 January 2027 in Edmonton and Red Deer." It is still unclear what consequences the CAS ruling will have for the men's ice hockey world championship in May in Germany. The German government may follow Canada's lead after teams and sponsors threatened a boycott. The German Ice Hockey Federation welcomed the decision on the junior worlds. "For our U20 team, the situation is now clear. That gives players and the coaching team the necessary peace for preparation, which begins in a few weeks," chairman Frank Lutz said in a statement. "The Canadian government has clearly taken a position, and many nations have shown their stance in recent weeks. We now also need to plan securely for our home world championship in May - for the teams, the fans and all partners. We therefore demand a timely clarification from the IIHF."

sports.title: USC’s Playoff Hopes Crash After Late Turnover By Jayden Maiava
sports.description: Wisconsin Badgers outside linebacker Sebastian Cheeks (15) sacks USC Trojans quarterback Jayden Maiava (14) during their game Oct. 24, 2026, at Camp Randall Stadium in Madison, Wisconsin. The USC Trojans’ dream of making the College Football Playoff died on a muddy field in Bloomington, Indiana. A promising drive that looked like it would tie the game ended with quarterback Jayden Maiava throwing a fatal interception. With six minutes and 35 seconds remaining at the one-yard line, Indiana’s Isaiah Jones intercepted the pass meant for Kayden Dixon-Wyatt. The Trojans dropped multiple interception opportunities, missed two field goals, and committed several penalties on special teams. The New York Post reported that these mistakes were especially perplexing since USC had just finished a second bye week during which coach Lincoln Riley vowed improved performance. Instead, the team converted only two of eleven third downs and faded badly in the fourth quarter. A Season of Missed Chances The loss to Indiana was a massive blow for a team that had just beaten then-No. 2 Ohio State two weeks earlier. The loss to Indiana likely ended any real shot at the playoff. Riley now sits at a record of 1-8 against ranked opponents on the road. Grant Wilson secured the victory for the Hoosiers by connecting with Charlie Becker on a 42-yard touchdown pass as three minutes and 30 seconds were left on the clock. USC simply could not answer the call when it mattered most. The team had put itself on the clock with “The Time Is Now” billboards around Los Angeles, yet they failed to get it done. Following kicker Caden Chittenden’s missed 27-yard field goal to the right, Riley dropped his shoulders on the sideline. That miss ended a drive that had reached Indiana’s 8-yard line, leaving the Trojans stuck at a 20-13 deficit. The errors on special teams were just the latest in a long line of mistakes. The situation got even stranger when a fan ran onto the field during a timeout and made a field goal. This bizarre moment highlighted the chaos that consumed the Trojans’ night. Riley had vowed to fix the issues after a devastating road loss to Wisconsin earlier in the season, but the same problems returned with a vengeance. The Cost of Failure When a team has as much talent as USC, losing 27-13 to a top-10 opponent is hard to explain. The Trojans (7-3 overall, 4-3 Big Ten) simply could not make the big plays needed to win. Indiana (9-1, 6-1) controlled the game when it counted. The loss raises serious questions about the future of the program in Los Angeles. Riley fell to 1-8 against ranked teams on the road, a stat that does not look good for his job security.

sports.title: YSU’s Regular Season Ends with Loss – What Awaits 8-3 Penguins on Selection Sunday?
sports.description: Youngstown State’s regular season came to a somewhat unceremonious close on Saturday evening. Illinois State quarterback Beckham Pellant lowered his shoulder and dove over the goal line with just nine seconds left to lift the Redbirds to a gutsy 34-33 win over the Penguins. YSU has no game next weekend so that was it, at least for the regular season. With eight wins, Beau Brungard and company will still surely be in the playoffs when the bracket gets released next Sunday. But with no further chances to build their resume, the Penguins can only wait it out and see how the chips will fall. Where… and perhaps more importantly… when will they play next? That’s the question that looms over Doug Phillips’ team right now. There is an argument to be made that they’ve done enough to avoid playing Thanksgiving weekend but also plenty to suggest that the bye week may also no longer be a possibility either. Youngstown State is 8-3 with all of their victories coming over DI teams. They have ranked wins over South Dakota, Southern Illinois, Northern Iowa and North Dakota. Two of those were Top 10 victories at the time. With all that it’s probably safe to say that they haven’t played their last home game. Whether or not it’s in the first or second round, though, will largely depend on what some of their counterparts do this next Saturday. They will want the race for the top eight seeds to remain as open as possible and thus will need some squads who are in a similar spot to lose. YSU will be rooting for the following teams this weekend: Montana State (vs. Montana) South Dakota (@ Illinois State) Northern Colorado (@ Northern Arizona) ETSU (@ Mercer) Central Arkansas (vs. Austin Peay) McNeese (vs. Lamar) If those listed teams win that keeps the 5-8 seed range quite a bit clearer for the Penguins to grab one of those spots. If that comes to pass they’d be the only group to have two weeks off before their first playoff game. Whether or not that’s a good thing is a whole different conversation. In the scenario that they do end up playing in the opening round, one would imagine that they’d receiver a higher seed in the 9-12 range. That would guarantee a home game likely against a lower conference champion from somewhere like the Ohio Valley or Pioneer League. Last year Youngstown State drew Ivy League winner Yale in the first round and it’s a game their fans would probably rather just forget. A positioning like that would set up a potential matchup against a lower-seeded bye week team if they were to advance. A second-round road trip against the likes of a Lamar, Montana, Austin Peay or Mercer is entirely possible in that case. Closing it out against Illinois State would have gone a long way in avoiding all this speculation. As of now, though, Youngstown State has left much of its postseason fate into the hands of others and the committee. There will be more football to be played nonetheless, though, and they will not have to sweat it out as a bubble team next week.

sports.title: Ronaldinho turns back the clock at 46 as the Brazil legend ends his 11-year exile with a stunning Ravenna comeback
sports.description: Ravenna v Forli: Serie C - Getty Images Sport Ronaldinho turned back the clock on Sunday, ending 11 years away from professional football with a sensational comeback for Ravenna at the age of 46. The Brazil legend started the Serie C derby against Forli in front of a sold-out crowd, showed flashes of his old magic and played a key part in the opening goal before being substituted at half-time. Ronaldinho starts for Ravenna in Forli derby Ronaldinho made his long-awaited comeback on Sunday, starting for Ravenna in their Serie C derby against Forli at a sold-out Stadio Bruno Benelli. The Brazilian had not played since leaving Fluminense in 2015, and came out of retirement for the third-tier club he joined as an investor in August. According to BBC Sport, he trained with his new team-mates only once, on Saturday, before the game. A team graphic had placed him on the left, but he spent most of his 45 minutes in a central role. Ronaldinho plays key part in Donati opener There were plenty of bright touches from the former Barcelona star, and he was involved in the opening goal. Ronaldinho held off a defender before playing the pass that came before the assist for Giulio Donati, who drove in a shot from outside the box. He had already carved out an earlier chance for the defender, swinging in a corner that Donati met with a header, only to see it saved. Ronaldinho was then substituted at the break, ending an outing that was streamed in several countries around the world. Dida joins Ronaldinho amid half-time frenzy The interval brought a media circus, with journalists surrounding Ronaldinho, and Dida, his former team-mate with Brazil and AC Milan, joined him on the pitch. A temporary stand, named the R10 after his famous shirt number, had been built for the fixture. In his prime, Ronaldinho won the 2002 World Cup with Brazil, the 2006 Champions League with Barcelona, and league titles with Barca and Milan. He also claimed the Ballon d'Or and FIFA World Player of the Year award in 2005, and played for Paris Saint-Germain, Gremio, Flamengo, Atletico Mineiro, Fluminense and Queretaro. Will Ronaldinho play for Ravenna again? Ronaldinho scored 299 goals in his career and had hoped to reach 300 in Ravenna colours, with the plan being for him to take a penalty had the hosts been awarded one. Whether he gets another chance remains unclear, as it is not yet known if he will play again for Ravenna, who sit second in their Serie C group.

sports.title: Move over, Peyton Manning! Josh Allen now owns another NFL record
sports.description: Nov 25, 2021; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen (17) gestures after throwing a touchdown pass in the fourth quarter against the New Orleans Saints at the Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Chuck Cook-USA TODAY Sports Josh Allen no longer has to share the top spot with Peyton Manning. The Buffalo Bills quarterback has officially moved ahead of the Pro Football Hall of Famer, becoming the NFL’s all-time leader in combined touchdowns by a quarterback through his first 10 seasons. And Allen has done it before completing his ninth year. And he did it in nine seasons. 😏 @JoshAllenQB | #BillsMafia pic.twitter.com/5PKNI0B5aX — Buffalo Bills (@BuffaloBills) November 15, 2026 Allen entered Sunday’s game against the New York Jets tied with Manning at 322 career touchdowns. One more touchdown was all he needed to claim the record for himself. On Buffalo’s second possession of the day, Allen methodically moved the Bills down the field. After a defensive holding call gave the Bills a first and goal at the one-foot line, Allen called his own number and used the opportunity to pass Manning. Josh Allen calls his own number. 😤 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/9Fj8amAJvc — Buffalo Bills (@BuffaloBills) November 15, 2026 With that touchdown, Allen’s career total climbed to 323, passing the mark Manning established during his first decade with the Indianapolis Colts. But the difference between the two quarterbacks isn’t just the number of touchdowns. It’s how quickly Allen got there. Manning needed 160 regular-season games to reach 322 touchdowns. Allen matched that total in just 136 games, throwing his record-tying touchdown against the Minnesota Vikings last Monday night. That’s 24 fewer games, the equivalent of nearly a season and a half of football. Allen has also taken a different route to the record. While Manning’s touchdowns came almost exclusively through the air, Allen has been just as dangerous with his legs. His career total entering Sunday included 232 passing touchdowns, 88 rushing touchdowns, and two receiving touchdowns. Patrick Mahomes is the only other active quarterback in the top 10 who can still add to his total. The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback entered Week 10 with 301 touchdowns and will spend the remainder of the season chasing Allen. But Mahomes is already in his 10th NFL season, meaning his final number will be set when the regular season ends in January. Allen, meanwhile, will have all of 2027 to keep adding to a record Mahomes will no longer be eligible to chase.

science.description: null You just ordered a Pizza Hut and a two-liter bottle of Mountain Dew. You put on "Space Jam" to watch the greatest of all time team up with the Looney Tunes. It's a perfect evening… in 1996 or 2026. The entire concept of "Space Jam" is so '90s that you swear you can hear Los Del Rio in the background mouthing, "Dale a tu cuerpo alegría, Macarena." As ridiculous as an intergalactic basketball match may sound, it's a perfect example of how even the strangest idea can work if you commit to it fully. In case you thought you hallucinated the whole thing, no, you didn't, as the Looney Tunes find themselves in quite the predicament in this live-action-animation hybrid. A bunch of aliens known as the Nerdlucks arrive on Earth to abduct the Tunes and take them back as attractions to the outer-space amusement park known as Moron Mountain (shockingly nobody has claimed that subreddit, so do your thing, Internet!). Being a wheeling-and-dealing wabbit, though, Bugs Bunny proposes a winner-takes-all basketball game between the Tunes and the tiny Nerdlucks. Unfortunately, the crafty aliens use their tech to steal the talent from ballers like Charles Barkley and Muggsy Bogues and turn themselves into the scary and skilled Monstars. So, Bugs and friends reach out to Michael Jordan, who recently switched from basketball to baseball, to help the Tune Squad win this intergalactic b-ball matchup and their freedom, because if anybody can do it, Air Jordan (Hare Jordan?) can. Oh, Bill Murray also shows up here a few times. Why? Because he can! (Image credit: Warner Bros. Pictures) "Space Jam" is a spin on the classic sci-fi trope of resolving high-stakes conflicts through sports. In 1975, "Death Race 2000" introduced a world where people drive like hooligans and bash into each other to get ahead and win races (ironically, this is the regular experience on any public road now). Meanwhile, in the same year, "Rollerball" demonstrated how to use extreme sports as a plot device whereby brutality trumped any kind of skill in the arena. Yet "Space Jam" took this concept, cartoonified it for a family-friendly audience, and challenged the conflict resolution approaches of other alien invasion movies from 1996. While " Independence Day " saw the heroes trying to destroy the mothership and "Mars Attacks" featured humans running away from "Ack! Ack"-ing extraterrestrials with ray guns, this film used the court to settle the score. It's an innovative way to deal with interplanetary matters, that's for sure. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 15, 1988: The 300-foot Green Bank Telescope collapses suddenly, leaving a huge pile of wreckage in West Virginia
science.description: null On Nov. 15, 1988, a 300-foot radio telescope in Green Bank, West Virginia suddenly collapsed. It happened at 9:46 p.m. on a clear night with no strong winds. When the observatory staff showed up to work the next morning, they were greeted by a huge pile of wreckage. The telescope collapsed under its own weight after a key structural element called a "gusset plate" failed. This was one of four connecting plates that held the telescope's large, metal beams together. Investigators found that these gusset plates were not built to last the 26 years that this telescope had been in use. Three years later, construction began on a new telescope. The Green Bank Telescope was even bigger and more sensitive, and it began science operations in 2001. (Image credit: NRAO/AUI/NSF) Why it mattered When the 300-foot telescope first debuted, it was not just the United States' largest radio observatory, but the largest such facility in the world. But its quick construction — just two years — led to it having to be significantly upgraded later. "In 1970, the 300-foot’s surface had become so warped from maintenance crews, snow, and its own weight that a new finer-meshed aluminum surface was installed," the website for the National Radio Astronomy Observatory reads. "A larger traveling feed was also installed at the prime focus." The collapse, however, was no one's fault. "Unforeseeable stress factors cracked a steel connector plate," wrote the NRAO. The Green Bank Telescope collapse left a mass of twisted debris behind. (Image credit: NRAO/AUI/NSF) During its years of observations, the 300-foot telescope contirbuted to the discovery of dark matter and the realization that pulsars come from supernova explosions. "One of the most important products to come out of the 300-foot telescope was an all-sky survey of radio objects called the Green Bank 6cm Survey. Nearly every northern hemisphere radio object studied by any other telescope is from a catalog compiled using this telescope," reads the NRAO website. Want more space history? science.title: Why hasn't the 'Blaze Star' exploded yet? Astronomers weigh in on what to expect
science.description: null For the past two years, stargazers have waited with bated breath for a "new" light to appear in the night sky, born of one of the most cataclysmic events known to occur in the cosmos — a nova explosion. But what is the "Blaze Star" T. Coronae Borealis, and why is it so difficult to predict when its overdue brightening will occur? We turned to the experts to find out. What is T. Coronae Borealis? T. Coronae Borealis — or T CrB for short — isn't a single star, but rather a binary system containing a dense white dwarf star and a bloated red giant. Over a period of around 80 years, the white dwarf's gravity strips material from the red giant until it hits a critical threshold. Next comes a dramatic nova explosion that causes the star to flare to 1,000 times its usual brightness before gradually settling down and repeating the cycle. Why is it so challenging to predict T. CrB's nova flare? "T CrB *will* erupt sometime soon," Bradley Schaefer of the Louisiana State University Department of Physics and Astronomy told Space.com in an email. "Everyone is very confident on this. But we cannot make high-accuracy measures of the rate of gas falling onto the surface of the white dwarf, and we do not have a high accuracy measure of the trigger mass for the big hydrogen bomb." Schaefer continued. Historical observations reveal that the last nova eruption reached Earth in 1946, which places us well inside the window for another dramatic brightening of T. CrBb. However, the unpredictability of the white dwarf's feeding makes it difficult to pin down exactly when the explosion will become visible from Earth. An animation of T. CrB brightening. (Image credit: NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center Conceptual Image Lab) "The exact date of the upcoming T CrB eruption depends primarily on how fast the gas coming from its companion star is accumulating on the surface of the white dwarf," explained Schaefer. "When some specific trigger mass has accumulated, then T CrB will erupt. For the last 80 years, we have been watching the gas pile up on the white dwarf surface, and we know that it must be near the trigger threshold." Astronomers have tried to predict T CrB's brightening by comparing a recent fluctuation in the light of the distant star system to a similar event that occurred in the runup to the 1946 event. "There have already been some dimming and brightening episodes that caused excitement but did not yet turn into the main event," Elizabeth Hays, lab chief at NASA's Astroparticle Physics Laboratory at the Goddard Spaceflight Center , told Space.com in an email. "It is likely that the nova will happen in the next few years but we still don't know exactly when. I can't give you a guaranteed prediction, but I will be a little surprised if it gets to 2030, or 84 years past the last eruption."
